fix(desktop): use meaningful message for fork session initialization

Replace empty string query with descriptive fork initialization message
when creating forked sessions. This prevents malformed session entries
that cause "cache_control cannot be set for empty text blocks" API errors
when resuming forked sessions.

The initialization message instructs Claude to acknowledge the forked
context and wait for user input, ensuring proper session registration
in Claude Code's internal index.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(desktop): properly fork sessions by copying JSONL and updating sessions-index

Previously, forking attempted to create a session via executeQuery and then
overwrite the JSONL file, but this caused issues:
- Empty text blocks from empty queries caused API errors
- The copied context was overwritten by Claude Code's new session
- Session wasn't properly registered in Claude Code's index

This change:
- Copies the parent JSONL file first, preserving full conversation context
- Updates sessions-index.json to register the forked session
- Skips executeQuery for cross-directory forks (no longer needed)
- Claude Code can now discover and resume forked sessions properly

The adapter now extracts metadata (firstPrompt, messageCount, gitBranch)
from the copied JSONL to populate the session index entry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(desktop): extract actual source cwd from JSONL when forking sessions

The previous implementation used process.cwd() as sourceWorkingDir, which
is the Electron app's working directory, not the source session's actual
working directory. This caused the cwd replacement to fail, leaving the
forked session with incorrect paths.

Now the adapter extracts the actual cwd from the source JSONL content,
ensuring paths are correctly transformed when forking to a new workspace.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(desktop): replace all cwds when forking sessions with fork history

Sessions that have been forked multiple times contain multiple different
cwds from their history. The previous fix only extracted and replaced the
first cwd found, leaving other paths unchanged.

Now extracts all unique cwds from the source JSONL and replaces each one
with the target working directory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(desktop): simplify cwd extraction to use single source workspace path

The fork adapter was incorrectly trying to extract and replace multiple cwds
from session history. A properly functioning session should only have one cwd
(the original workspace path). Multiple cwds were artifacts from previous
broken fork implementations.

Simplified extractAllCwdsFromContent() back to extractCwdFromContent() which
returns the first cwd found in the JSONL file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(desktop): find session file using sourceWorkingDir to avoid wrong source

The findSessionFile method was searching all project directories and returning
the first match. Since the same session ID can exist across multiple project
folders (from previous forks), this caused the wrong source file to be copied.

Now findSessionFile uses sourceWorkingDir to look in the correct project folder
first, falling back to searching all directories for backwards compatibility.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(desktop): add sourceWorkspacePath to ForkOptions for correct session lookup

The fork operation was using process.cwd() as the source workspace path,
which returns the Electron app's directory instead of the actual source
session's workspace. This caused the wrong JSONL file to be copied when
multiple project folders had files with the same session ID.

Changes:
- Added sourceWorkspacePath field to ForkOptions interface
- ForkService now passes request.repoPath as sourceWorkspacePath
- ClaudeCodeAgent.forkSession uses sourceWorkspacePath for correct lookup

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(desktop): filter only matches user/assistant message uuids

The filter was incorrectly matching file-history-snapshot entries that share
the same messageId as the target user message. This caused the filter to stop
early before the actual target message was included.

Now matchesMessageId() only matches uuid for user/assistant type messages,
ignoring metadata entries like file-history-snapshot that may share messageId.

* refactor(canvas): extract state into dedicated hooks

Extract all useState calls from Canvas.tsx into dedicated state hooks
following the project's component architecture principle.

New hooks created:
- useGithubUser: GitHub username fetching with loading/error states
- useCanvasUIState: Modal states (settings, command palette, new agent)
- useContextMenu: Context menu position and click-outside handling
- useAutoFork: Auto-fork setting with localStorage persistence
- useKeyboardModifiers: Node drag enable and shift key tracking
- usePendingAgent: Pending agent position, linear issue, worktree flag
- useLinearPanel: Linear panel collapse and resize states

Canvas.tsx changes:
- Remove ~15 useState calls
- Remove ~4 useEffect blocks now handled by hooks
- Remove duplicate callback definitions
- Remove unused imports and type definitions

Extract canvas hooks from renderer/hooks to features/canvas/hooks for
better feature-based organization:

- useCanvasActions: canvas node creation actions
- useCanvasDrop: drag/drop handling for Linear issues
- useCanvasPersistence: canvas state persistence
- useCanvasUIState: modal and overlay states
- useContextMenu: right-click menu state
- useForkModal: fork modal operations
- useKeyboardModifiers: keyboard modifier tracking
- usePendingAgent: pending agent creation state

Update hooks/index.ts to re-export from features/canvas/hooks
maintaining backward compatibility for existing imports.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(hooks): migrate feature hooks to zustand stores

Migrate 9 state hooks in the features folder to use Zustand for global
state management. This provides better state sharing across components
and eliminates prop drilling.

Hooks migrated:
- useCanvasUIState (modals/overlays)
- useKeyboardModifiers (drag/shift states)
- usePendingAgent (pending agent creation)
- useSidebarState (collapse/width)
- useContextMenu (context menu position + click-outside)
- useFolderHighlight (folder colors + highlight toggle)
- useLinearPanel (collapse/resize)
- usePillState (animation states)

All hooks maintain backwards-compatible API surfaces. Hooks with DOM
effects use a hybrid pattern: Zustand store for state + React wrapper
for refs and effects.

Also fixes:
- Import paths for MessagePreview type
- Import path for ILinearStore
- Duplicate LinearIssue export conflict

Add custom lint script to detect and prevent `if (...) return undefined`

This enforces the project rule: "Never use defensive defaults."

fix: prevent infinite loop when deleting last canvas node (#52)

Extract unhighlight logic into pure function `removeHighlightStylesFromNodes`
that returns the same array reference when no changes are needed. This prevents
React from detecting false state changes that caused infinite re-render loops.

The bug occurred because:
1. unhighlightAllAgentNodes always returned a new array via .map()
2. When nodes was empty [], map() returned new [] reference
3. React detected "state change", triggered re-render
4. useEffect ran again -> infinite loop

* fix: filter stale sdk permission events on app startup

When the app starts and the SDK connects to existing sessions, stale
permission requests (like unanswered AskUserQuestion prompts) from
session history get re-emitted. This caused old clarifying questions
to appear in the ActionPill after app restart.

Root cause: The Claude Code SDK re-emits pending permission requests
when connecting to sessions that have unanswered prompts in their
JSONL history.

Fix: Add a 3-second startup grace period during which SDK permission
events are ignored. This filters stale events while allowing legitimate
new permission requests (which only occur after user interaction).

Also adds diagnostic logging to trace event sources for future debugging.
